text:
alex: Quick heads-up — proposing a split-shift maintenance for az3 and az7 to rebalance GPU pool thresholds. Target window: 00:00-03:00 UTC next Tue. Rolling cordon + soft-drain, canary on 5 nodes per AZ.

maria: Why split-shift vs single window?

alex: To avoid overlapping with EU morning traffic and US late-night spike. We do az3 (EU) 00:00-01:30, az7 (US) 01:30-03:00. Keeps global capacity smoother.

sam: What’s the expected capacity hit? rough numbers pls.

alex: Plan holds ~10% of each pool offline during drain; canary nodes will be isolated first. Net impact on hosted capacity ~6% during handoff.

leo: Any tenants we should pin or migrate ahead of time?

alex: Priority tenants pinned via routing policy: tenant-ml-prod, realtime-search. We'll add temporary route weight to fallback pools.

priya: Cost ask — will this trigger burst on dedicated / reserved that increases bill?

alex: Might cause short-term burst for hosted fallback; expect ~2–4% extra GPU minutes for 3h. Nominal. Recommend enabling autoscale cap to limit spend.

maria: Canary plan + rollback?

alex: Canary sequence: cordon 5 nodes -> soft-drain non-interruptible jobs -> run health checks + KV cache seed -> run small sample queries through canary -> promote. If errors >3% or latency +200ms for 5m -> abort and rollback by uncordon.

sam: How are we seeding KV cache? commands?

alex: Using the canary-seed job, example: 

```
kubectl label node n-canary-01 canary=true
kubectl cordon n-canary-01
jobctl start canary-seed --nodes n-canary-01 --workload embed-sample
```

leo: Will streaming jobs be affected?

alex: Streaming requests routed away during soft-drain. We’ll set short-lived fallback to smaller LLM variant to keep p99 latency SLAs.

priya: Who’s on-call? need an incident owner.

alex: Sam and Leo will be on-call for the window. Priya you own spend guard (autoscale caps). Maria will handle customer comms.

sam: Noted. I’ll set up a quick dashboard for canary metrics (latency, error-rate, GPU-util) and an alert: errors >2% sustained 3m.

infra-bot: Deploy job queued: maintenance-notify-1769009999 -> 6 subsystems. Reminder scheduled 24h and 1h before window.

alex: We should also run a dry-run tonight in staging with identical routing rules.

maria: Will craft customer blurb: 1) brief impact 2) expected times 3) how to reach support. Posting to status page + in-console banner.

sam: Quick question on fairness: are we adjusting tenant weights to avoid eviction noise?

alex: Yes — lowering eviction aggressiveness and adjusting fairness_shift threshold to 0.15 during drain. That reduces churn but increases spill to fallback pools.

leo: Any manual steps if canary fails?

alex: Rollback play: uncordon canary nodes, flush cache, re-route traffic back, and escalate to runtime team if KV seed error. Estimated RTO 20–30m.

priya: I’ll put an autoscale cap at +10% and add budget alert at +5% above expected.

maria: Done. Draft status note ready, will annotate with region-specific times (local).

sam: I’ll add a small script to drain only non-latency-critical queues first. snippet: 

```
for q in lowprio queues; do jobctl drain --queue $q --strategy soft; done
```

alex: Thanks. Action items:
- sam: dashboard + drain script (due EOD)
- maria: status + console banner (due EOD)
- priy a: set autoscale cap & budget alerts (done before window)
- leo: run staging dry-run tonight and report

leo: Will run at 20:00 UTC and post results.

alex: If no objections by EOD I’ll schedule the maintenance and ping infra-bot to send notifications.

maria: LGTM. :thumbsup:

sam: LGTM.

infra-bot: Notification sent to #customers-status and support rotation assigned.

alex: Closing loop — create follow-up thread for post-maint metrics and regression-check once done.

maria: Thanks team.
